summary: T6 lands the redirect_uri allowlist, PKCE-state binding to redirect_uri, and the BootstrapTickets LRU+TTL store + endpoints cleanly. Implementation closely mirrors the existing PendingBundles pattern, all 13 task-spec tests pass, clippy with -D warnings is clean, and the 12 baseline test failures (9 lib + 3 integration) are confirmed pre-existing — they trace to a prior switch from sign_cose/verify_artifact to raw verify_signature in authorize_handler that left legacy COSE-based tests stale, plus an oauth_flow integration test in the same shape, plus a pending_authz allowlist mismatch from Decision 12. T6 only added a positional `Vec::new()` arg to oauth_flow.rs to keep it compiling. Minor concerns: redirect_uri-on-/token is Option (acknowledged in decisions, tracked as backlog hardening for client_id=mnemonic-cli); no body-size cap on /issue keypair_json; pubkey-derive uses unwrap_or_default; tests for /issue and /redeem don't exercise the real production router. None block merge.

stats.tests_status: 13/13 task-spec tests pass; 12 pre-existing failures verified baseline (not introduced by T6)

findings.title: redirect_uri on /oauth/token is Option, not required for client_id=mnemonic-cli
findings.details: TokenRequest::redirect_uri is `#[serde(default)] Option<String>` and the equality check only runs when the field is supplied. Per RFC 6749 §4.1.3, when the authorize request supplied a redirect_uri (the case for every entry on the new allowlist), the token request MUST include the identical value. The current implementation accepts a missing field as a pass — defeating the binding for any attacker who leaks a code and chooses to omit the field. Decisions log #3 acknowledges this and defers to a future hardening pass. For mnemonic-cli specifically the CLI should always send redirect_uri; the spec (Decision 5) literally says 'token-exchange validates that verifier, state, and redirect_uri all match'.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) require redirect_uri unconditionally, OR (b) require it specifically when issued.code_challenge was paired with a non-empty issued.redirect_uri AND the bound URI was a CLI/loopback scheme. Capture the deferral as an explicit backlog item and add a `// TODO Decision 5 hardening` marker so this isn't lost. Mitigation: Phase-1 attack model requires both leaking the auth code AND knowing the bound redirect_uri's existence; capability is bounded by the 60s code TTL (CODE_TTL_SECS).

findings.title: /api/cli-bootstrap/issue accepts unbounded keypair_json size
findings.details: BootstrapIssueRequest::keypair_json is taken verbatim into BootstrapTicket and bounded only by axum's default 2 MB request-body limit. PendingBundles has explicit MAX_CONTENT_BYTES (32KB) and MAX_METADATA_BYTES (4KB) caps to bound LRU memory. With per-user cap 3 + LRU 100, a malicious authenticated user could pin ~600 MB of memory per ticket-batch by issuing maximally-sized payloads. A real Solana keypair JSON is ~200 bytes.
findings.recommendation: Add a hard cap (suggest 4 KB) on keypair_json at the top of bootstrap_issue_handler, similar to PendingBundles' size checks. Reject with 413 Payload Too Large. Optional: validate it parses as a JSON array of 64 numbers at issue time so the redeem handler never returns 500 on malformed payloads (closes F4 too).

findings.title: bootstrap_redeem_handler silently substitutes all-zeros pubkey on derive failure
findings.details: `solana_sdk::pubkey::Pubkey::try_from(&bytes[32..64]).map(...).unwrap_or_default()` swallows the error and emits the all-zeros pubkey. Pubkey::try_from from a 32-byte slice should never fail in practice (the slice length matches), but if it does the CLI receives a misleading response with status 200 and a sentinel pubkey. The right behavior is 500 — same as the bytes.len()/serde_json::from_str failure paths above.
findings.recommendation: Replace `.unwrap_or_default()` with an explicit match returning a 500 like the prior arms. Or use `.expect("32-byte slice cannot fail Pubkey::try_from")` if the guarantee is structural — pick one or the other consistently.

findings.title: stored keypair_json parse error message echoes attacker-controlled content via 500
findings.details: If keypair_json was issued with garbage content (per F2 there is no validation at issue time), the redeem handler returns 500 with `format!("stored keypair_json is not a JSON byte array: {e}")`. The serde_json error message can include the offending input bytes. Minor info-leak — content is owned by the issuing user themselves, but error message exposure to the redeem caller (who in honest flow is the same user) is a stylistic concern.
findings.recommendation: Validate at issue time (closes F2 + F4 simultaneously) and turn the redeem-side parse error into an opaque 500 (`"internal: stored keypair malformed"`). Log the detailed error server-side via `tracing::error!`.

findings.title: Bootstrap-redeem HTTP tests use a copy-paste handler, not the production handler
findings.details: test_bootstrap_redeem_no_auth_required and test_bootstrap_redeem_unknown_ticket_404 build a synthetic axum router that wraps a hand-rolled `redeem` closure mirroring bootstrap_redeem_handler — not the actual handler. Comment acknowledges the choice ('full McpState is unwieldy to mock here'). Risk: divergence between the test handler and bootstrap_redeem_handler is invisible to CI. The `mock_state` helper in test_support.rs already wires in BootstrapTickets, so a real-handler integration test in `mcp/tests/` would be feasible.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal integration test in `mcp/tests/bootstrap_tickets.rs` that uses `test_support::mock_state()` and calls `api::bootstrap_redeem_handler` directly, asserting the same observables (status 200 with secret/pubkey shape, status 404 on unknown UUID). Optional follow-up; current unit tests still cover the LRU/TTL/cap semantics.

findings.title: Per-user cap and atomic-consume tests do not assert through the HTTP layer
findings.details: test_bootstrap_ticket_per_user_cap directly asserts `Err(BootstrapInsertError::PerUserCapExceeded)` rather than confirming the handler maps it to HTTP 429. The 429 mapping (api.rs:286-295) is conditional logic only exercised at handler-level — a refactor swapping 429/503 mappings would slip past this test. Same for the LruExhausted variant (line 296-302) which is documented as currently unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Add a single handler-level test that drives 4 inserts via bootstrap_issue_handler with a synthesized Claims extension and asserts response.status() == 429. Optional polish; current store-level coverage is correct.

findings.title: /api/cli-bootstrap/* routes have no rate limiter
findings.details: The api_subrouter in main.rs only applies bearer_auth_middleware. /api/cli-bootstrap/redeem/:ticket is on the bearer-auth allowlist (no JWT), so an unauthenticated attacker can spam it with random UUIDs. Each request takes a tokio mutex on BootstrapTickets, attempts a UUID parse, then an LRU pop. Bounded but unrate-limited. /api/cli-bootstrap/issue is JWT'd + per-user-capped at 3, so abuse there is bounded by a single user's cap.
findings.recommendation: Apply the existing GovernorLayer (mcp_governor_conf) to api_subrouter, OR define a separate governor for /api/cli-bootstrap/redeem/* with a tight per-IP cap (e.g., 10/min) — same shape as the oauth governor.

findings.title: Insert eviction-account branch is mostly-dead
findings.details: `if guard.lru.peek(&ticket_id).is_some() || evicted.jwt_sub != jwt_sub` always short-circuits true on the first arm because `ticket_id` is a freshly minted UUIDv4 and was just `push`ed — `peek(&ticket_id).is_some()` cannot be false. The condition's second arm (`evicted.jwt_sub != jwt_sub`) is therefore unreachable. The 'defensively skip' comment acknowledges this. The same pattern in PendingBundles (pending.rs:243-250) has the same defensive shape. Not a bug, just dead code preserved for symmetry.
findings.recommendation: Either drop the `if`-guard (always call `dec_user`), or document with a single-line comment that the arm exists only for symmetry with PendingBundles. Cosmetic.

findings.title: BootstrapInsertError::LruExhausted variant is unreachable production code
findings.details: Decision 7 spec asks for a 503 mapping for total-LRU-full, but `LruCache::push` always evicts the oldest entry to make room — production code never returns LruExhausted. The variant is `#[allow(dead_code)]` and the handler has a 503 arm that is never taken. Decisions log #5 acknowledges this as documented dead code.
findings.recommendation: OK as-is. Document the rationale in the variant doc-comment more explicitly OR remove the variant entirely (and the 503 handler arm) and rely on the per-user 429 as the only insert-error path. Strictly cosmetic; the `#[allow(dead_code)]` is correct.

good_practices: is_loopback_callback hand-rolled rather than pulling in a regex crate — concise, no new dependency, covered by 8+ unit-test cases including lookalike-host attack (127.0.0.1.evil.com) and missing-port edge cases.
allowed_redirect cleanly separates exact-match / exact-prefix / loopback-with-client-id-gate — readable and matches the task spec one-to-one.
BootstrapTickets::new(...) wraps lru_capacity.max(1) in NonZeroUsize::expect — same defensive pattern as PendingBundles::new, cannot panic on legitimate inputs.
Atomic consume under a single tokio::sync::Mutex guard — concurrent two-thread test (test_bootstrap_ticket_atomic_consume) confirms exactly-one-Some semantics.
force_expire test helper avoids real-time clock dependency — same approach as PendingBundles::force_expire.
404 envelope on bootstrap_not_found is uniform across not-found / consumed / expired — defeats probing-attacker distinguishability.
redirect_uri stored on IssuedCode is bound at code-issue time and validated on token-exchange — closes RFC 6749 §4.1.3 swap-redirect attack.

test_oauth_state_binding_validates_redirect_uri_too explicitly tests that a 400 mismatch ALSO consumes the code (single-use semantic) — security-property documentation that future refactors can't accidentally weaken.
Bearer-auth allowlist correctly exempts only `/api/cli-bootstrap/redeem/` (with trailing slash) — `/issue` is not on the list.
Lock discipline mirrors PendingBundles — no .await held while the mutex guard is alive.

BootstrapTicket::ticket_id and PendingAuthorize::challenge_hash both correctly carry `#[allow(dead_code)]` for fields retained for future audit/log continuity — same convention used elsewhere in the crate.
Per-user counter properly decrements on (a) successful consume, (b) expired consume, (c) LRU eviction of an unrelated entry — three-way accounting consistency mirrors PendingBundles.

baseline_failures_verified.claim: 9 pre-existing lib failures + 2 integration failures, confirmed via git stash
baseline_failures_verified.verification_method: Inspected mcp/src/oauth.rs in commit 3e0752c~1 (parent) — production authorize_handler already uses identity::verify_signature (raw 64-byte Ed25519); test code still builds COSE_Sign1 envelopes via sign_cose. T6 commit only removed an unused `verify_artifact` import (which clippy -D warnings forces). Test/production drift is pre-existing.
baseline_failures_verified.discrepancy: Decisions log mentions 2 integration; we observe 3. The third (oauth_flow.rs) is in the same shape as the lib-test failures (raw-Ed25519 vs COSE_Sign1 drift) — likely conflated with the lib count by T6. Material to nobody — none introduced by T6.
baseline_failures_verified.verdict: ACCEPTED — failures predate T6 and trace to a prior raw-Ed25519 migration that left legacy COSE-based tests stale. T6 only added the positional `Vec::new()` arg to oauth_flow.rs to keep it compiling.

recommendations_for_t7_or_followup: F1 should be tracked as a `// TODO RFC 6749 §4.1.3 hardening` in oauth.rs and added to backlog.md as a security-debt item.
F2 + F4 can be closed together by validating keypair_json shape at issue time (4KB cap + JSON-array-of-64-numbers parse).
F5 + F6 can be addressed by adding mcp/tests/bootstrap_tickets.rs (real-handler integration test) — small lift, large signal.
F7 should be addressed before public deploy — even a 10-req/min per-IP governor on /api/cli-bootstrap/redeem closes the spam vector.
Pre-existing 12 baseline failures (9 lib + 3 integration) need separate cleanup task — out of scope for T6 but blocking pre-deploy QA.
notes: Implementation quality is high — the BootstrapTickets store is a careful clone of PendingBundles' established LRU+TTL+per-user-cap pattern, and the redirect_uri allowlist is implemented as a small, well-tested standalone function with 8+ negative test cases including subtle host-prefix and port-format attacks. All 13 task-spec tests pass; clippy and rustfmt are clean. Ship it; address the 9 minor findings in T7 / a hardening pass.
